entry.title: Combined summary - BIP 119 CTV activation client
entry.summary: Significant advancements have been implemented to support the deployment of CheckTemplateVerify (CTV, BIP-119), aimed at improving accessibility and clarity for both developers and users. A direct link to the activation client’s repository is now featured on the project website, streamlining access to essential tools and documentation. The repository can be accessed at [https://github.com/ctv-activation/activation-client](https://github.com/ctv-activation/activation-client). Detailed deployment specifications have been established, with the process commencing on 30 March 2026 and concluding on 30 March 2027. The scheduled minimum activation height is set at 1001952, anticipated to occur by May 2027. To foster robust community consensus, a 90% threshold over 2016 blocks has been mandated. An archival resource has also been provided ([archive.is/o6QgT](https://archive.is/o6QgT)), offering a comprehensive snapshot of the project's development and decision-making history. Despite these structured preparations, the broader Bitcoin community remains cautious about the CTV proposal, especially regarding its activation schedule. The skepticism largely arises from the absence of compelling, user-centric demonstrations that showcase CTV's advantages in real-world contexts, particularly during periods of elevated transaction fees. To bridge this gap, attention must shift toward the development and dissemination of software that not only utilizes CTV but also allows users to independently evaluate its effectiveness in high-fee scenarios. Demonstrating practical benefits through accessible, hands-on tools is fundamental to fostering greater acceptance and trust within the community. For a demonstration to be genuinely persuasive, it should facilitate reproducible comparisons rather than simply exhibiting a functional CTV transaction. In high-fee environments, thorough demonstrations would involve publishing detailed setup information and providing direct comparisons between the on-chain costs—such as weight and fees—of CTV-enabled transactions versus traditional alternatives achieving the same outcomes. This includes accounting for all relevant setup or recovery processes. Such rigorous evaluations help determine whether CTV fundamentally alters the economic landscape for users, moving beyond theoretical expressiveness to tangible cost savings and efficiency gains. Furthermore, consensus cannot be gauged solely by the absence of dissent in a single discussion thread; broad community engagement and readiness require more substantial evidence of support.
